newsitem.title: USA: U.S. states say progress made to tobacco deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. states say progress made to tobacco deal.

text.p: The chief negotiator for states in talks with cigarette companies on a settlement of lawsuits said tremendous progress had been made but no announcement of an agreement was likely on Thursday.

"We have met continuously today. We have made tremendous progress today ... We got more concessions from the industry today," Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore told reporters outside a Washington hotel where negotiators are meeting.
"We are very optimistic that we can resolve this matter very, very soon," Moore said. "There will be no announcement of any resolution today."

He said negotiators would continue working late on Thursday night and would resume talks on Friday. They are trying to reach an historic settlement of suits filed by 40 states to recoup the costs of treating sick smokers, as well as some class action suits.

Moore said he had briefed the White House on the status of the talks Thursday. President Bill Clinton is monitoring the negotiations because he and Congress would have to approve any deal before it could be implemented.
"I had a very positive meeting at the White House today, and I am happy with the help that the White House has given us," Moore said.
